An ordinal has no comparative (Mistrík p. 49): no exponent of rule:sk-no-degree names the cell, so a paradigm lists none.
Vianoce has no singular (Mistrík p. 27).
A modal verb gives no command.
`own` reads a value a default gives: kosa is feminine by its -a.
`own` reads a value the entry stores over the default (vlada stores Masc); a comma is one of them.
The most specific default wins, read as the pipeline reads it: -óva (written with its mark) over -a.
An ending written with a mark needs it: tova does not end in -óva, so -a's default holds.
A default with no ending holds of every noun the others leave.
Two free forms of a cell are no tie: the first is the form, the others come back as `free`.
A phrase's word realised alone (a reflexive verb's token writes the verb): the rules read that word as the form.
Its other word: no rule holds of sa (its `ends` reads the word), so nothing is given.
The phrase whole, no word named: as before, the rules read the whole form, and none holds of it (it ends in sa).
